newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Activity heats up.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Activity heats up.

text.p: Asian debt markets were unusually busy on Tuesday, with a slew of deals launching.
The day started off with a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue for Rizal Commercial Bank launched via LTCB Asia.

The deal has a five-year final maturity but can be put or called on the third anniversary. It pays a coupon of 75 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 87 basis points.
That's much tighter than Rizal's previous FRCD this year, which paid 118.33 basis points all-in for a straight three-year.
Bankers have complained that prices for Philippine issues have tightened too quickly and that the paper is not performing well in the secondary market.
Still, many investors remain bullish on the Philippine economy and say they are happy to hold the country's debt paper if the price is right and may be willing to if the price is almost right.
Another Philippine bank, Far East Bank and Trust, was out with a US$100 million multi-series FRCD. Sakura Finance Asia and Citicorp International are bookrunners.
Banks must participate in the three "series" on a more or less pro rate basis. The series have maturities of one, four and five years.
Fees for co-lead managers committing US$5-6 million are 15 basis points on a blended basis for an all-in return of approximately 89.86 basis points.
Fees for co-managers committing US$3-4 million are 12.05 basis points on a blended basis for an all-in return of approximately 88.86 basis points.
The average life of the transaction is 3.45 years.
In May, Far East Bank set an five-year put three FRCD that paid an all-in of 91.6 basis points to the top tier.
Angkasa Marketing, a subsidiary of Malaysia's Amsteel, launched a US$105 million FRN through arrangers Sanwa International Finance Hong Kong, BNP Singapore and Amsteel Corporate Finance Hong Kong.
The three-year paper pays an all-in of 136.6 basis points over LIBOR.
Among other Malaysian deals, the global bond for state-oil company Petronas is expected to launch very soon.
In London, Indonesia's Mulia Land raised US$200 million split evenly between a five-year fixed-rate Eurobond and a three-year floating rate note.
The bond will be priced to yield 290 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, while the FRN pays a margin of 225 basis points over LIBOR.
Mulia Land is primarily engaged in the property business.
